reading content splits evenly between the two slots and a rater reading position does not.

fail separately: claude-sonnet-5 reads position on `reaches` in the round-2 bundle
(p = 0.000825) while its `preference` votes in the same bundle are clean (p = 0.761).

ONE ENTRY HERE IS CONSERVATIVE AND IS MARKED SO. claude-opus-5's reach axis measures
p = 0.00144 on the deduplicated records, which does NOT clear ALPHA = 0.001. The paper
(app:a7) reports it at p = 1.1e-4 and quarantines it, and the shipped rows carry no opus
votes. The discrepancy is n: the paper's figure predates the dedup. Keeping the quarantine
changes no published number; lifting it would add a fifth rater to round-1 majorities and
move the headline agreement figure, which is a research decision and not a promote-time
one. `check_quarantine` therefore ACCEPTS an over-strict entry and records it, and hard
fails only the unsafe direction: a rater NOT quarantined here that reads position on
`preference`, the axis that decides a pair.
gpt-5.6-terra is not listed because it never rated a shipped bundle. It is pinned in .env
as PI_MODEL_ANNOTATOR and every pass must override it: it was quarantined on an earlier A7
pass at p ~ 4e-11 while catching 99 of 99 planted foils.
PANEL 2 (this file only; `quarantine.json` is untouched and both panels stay computable
from the same immutable root).
`gpt-oss-120b` is dropped from `preference` and `reaches` on all five A7 bundles. This is
NOT a slot-bias finding -- it is clean on every slot test it has been given (round 1:
preference p = 0.47, reaches p = 0.0343; round 2: preference p = 0.356, reaches p = 0.051).
It is a PANEL DEFINITION, and the measured reason is:
* It is near chance against the consequence rule. MEASURED 2026-09-14 on the 2,292
`ask_ask` pairs of data/rl/pairs.jsonl where all three raters voted a side:
* It disagrees with both other raters more than they disagree with each other. On the
same rows: sonnet vs gemini 77.1%, sonnet vs oss 65.5%, gemini vs oss 59.0%. On 2-1
splits it is the odd one out 602 of 1,127 times.
* It is the pinned Inquirer/Drafter/Answerer that GENERATED every question it rates, so
its agreement with the label is confounded with the corpus by construction. A reviewer
will name that confound; the paper names it first and reports both panels.
The decision (user, 2026-09-14) is to REPLACE it rather than add a fourth rater: a fourth
leaves the confounded votes inside the majority, adds 2-2 ties, and costs the same. Its
replacement is `gpt-5.6-sol-mirrored`, whose records are the order-consistent merge of
gpt-5.6-sol rated in both side orders (campaign panel2/, see that directory's README).
These five entries are OVER-STRICT BY DESIGN and `check_quarantine` accepts them as such:
a rater quarantined on an axis whose p sits above ALPHA is recorded `conservative` and the
promote continues -- it discards evidence rather than admitting bad evidence. Expect all
ten (5 bundles x 2 axes) to come back marked `conservative` in the promote manifest's
`slot_bias` block. That is the check working, not a warning.
NOTHING IS ADDED FOR `gpt-5.6-sol-mirrored`. The round-1 entry names `gpt-5.6-sol`, and
`promote.rater_of` keys the merged records under a different string on purpose, so the
raw round-1 quarantine does not reach votes that passed the order-consistency test. If
the MERGED records read position, the entry is added then, on that measurement.
PANEL 2, THE `a6` AXIS (added 2026-09-17). The five entries above withdraw `gpt-oss-120b`
from `preference` and `reaches`, which are A7 axes. They do NOT reach `a6` -- the CANDIDATE
RANKING axis that orders `pairs.rater.jsonl` -- so with only those entries the replacement
was carried out on the reaches ordering and never on the rater one. MEASURED 2026-09-17:
`data/rl/a6_preferences.jsonl` (4,610 verdicts, digest 0fce532025625f94) is byte-identical
under both panels and 4,476 of its rows still carry the withdrawn rater, under TWO spellings
(`gpt-oss-120b` on 4,249 and `oss` on 227; no row carries both, so matching the long form
alone understates it by 227).

THE BACKING IS A POSITION MEASUREMENT, NOT `_slot_bias`. `_slot_bias` has no A6 branch at
all (`fields = {"A7": ...}.get(task_type)` returns None and it returns `{}`), and
`check_quarantine` builds its per-bundle table from records with `task_type == "A7"` only.
So an `a6` entry is neither backed nor refused by that check -- and two of these three
bundles carry no A7 item whatever (A6 + A3_node only), so it never visits them. The check
will pass silently on these entries; that is a coverage gap, not a clearance.
A6 prints its candidates in a fixed order, so the analogue of a slot effect is: over every
ordered slot pair (i<j) the rater separated, how often did the EARLIER slot win? Content
gives ~0.5. MEASURED over all five A6 bundles, two-sided binomial against 0.5:
gpt-oss-120b     4,627/8,579 = 0.5393   p = 3.2e-13    <- reads position
Per bundle for `gpt-oss-120b`, against ALPHA = 0.001:
Two of the three entries below are therefore CONSERVATIVE in the sense this file already
uses for A7: an axis whose per-bundle p sits above alpha discards evidence rather than
admitting bad evidence. The pooled statistic is what backs the panel decision, and it is a
STRONGER finding than the one the panel was built on: the rater does not merely sit near
chance against the rule on this axis, it reads the printed order of the candidates -- which
an A7-only slot gate could not have seen.
STILL NOT WITHDRAWN ON `a6`: `musique-20260909-abda79de97eb` (fixed1, 223 A6 items) and
`musique-20260909-c8c7f315231c` (fixed2, 226). Both are BACKED or near it above, and both
carry A6 items that feed `promote.a6_verdicts` -- 6,746 preferences available against the
4,610 installed. Their A6 preferences are not part of the shipped instrument, so they do not
change the rater ORDERING, but a promote under this file will still count the withdrawn
rater into the `a6_*` fields it attaches. Add them when the panel-2 promote runs.
THE REPLACEMENT DOES NOT COVER THIS AXIS YET. `gpt-5.6-sol-mirrored` has 5,479 records and
every one is A7; it has no A6 vote at all. Until it does, withdrawing `gpt-oss-120b` here
leaves TWO raters, and a strict majority of two is agreement-only -- a different aggregation
rule, not the same instrument with a rater removed. Nothing is installed on these entries
until the replacement's A6 records land.
TWO DEFECTS IN THIS PANEL'S A7 MERGE, MEASURED 2026-09-17 AND DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED HERE.
Recorded so the next auditor meets them as known facts rather than rediscovering them as a
scare. Re-measure with `measure_shipped_merge_defects.py` (kept beside this campaign's A6
scratch); the repair is routed separately because it means regenerating something the paper
cites.
(1) AN INHERITED `item_set_hash`. The panel-2 `a7sub` and `-mirror` bundles copied the
source manifest's `item_set_hash` while shipping a SUBSET (a7sub) or a transformed set
(-mirror) of its items, so each disagrees with its own items and `validate_records`
refuses records against it as 'collected against a different build of this bundle'.
SCOPE: 11 files, every one under a raw/ SUBDIRECTORY that `promote.load_root` never
reads (10 in panel2/raw/, 1 in panel2dev/raw/). Under `bundles/`, which IS read, the
only mismatch is `suggest-20260904-2ba5dc3ac0cd.json` (`item_set_hash: null`), the
pilot the root README already marks NOT a validator.
WHAT IT DOES NOT COST: nothing that votes is untraceable. All 5,479 shipped merged
records carry the ORIGINAL bundle_id, so they join the immutable bundle whose hash is
correct, and all 5,479 re-derive their `prompt_sha` from the immutable item; all 5,693
a7sub items are byte-identical to the immutable ones. No reported n moves.
WHAT IT DOES COST: the MIRROR half. A merged record names a `mirror_record_id` under
`<bid>-mirror`, a bundle existing only in raw/ with the wrong hash, so re-deriving the
merge from its own inputs needs a file the validator refuses. Audit-time, not data.
(2) OVER-CAP CONCATENATED RATIONALES. The merge writes
`orig + ' || mirror: ' + mirror`, and two rationales each already clamped to 400 exceed
`RATIONALE_MAX_CHARS`. 3,864 of 6,302 merged records over cap (3,365 train + 499 dev),
longest 622. LOSSLESS: the string is exactly that concatenation on 5,479/5,479 train
records, and 0 of 11,386 raw per-order records were truncated, so no rater's reasoning
was cut before it was read. No computation reads the field -- the constant declares it
'explanatory metadata, never a label'.
THE VALIDATOR IS NOT THE DEFECT, AND WAS MEASURED BEFORE BEING BLAMED. Over the whole
immutable root the over-cap branch fires on 0 of 51,346 pass-produced records and on
3,864 of 6,302 records in the six merged files. A clamped rationale is <= 400 BY
CONSTRUCTION (`clamp_rationale` is `[:397].rstrip() + '...'`, verified exhaustively over
input lengths 1..3000), so the branch can never fire on one and there is no
false-positive class to separate. Exempting the field would delete the check's only true
positives. The out-of-contract records are the merge's doing and the repair belongs
there. The A6 half of this panel already does it the other way: `rationale` is the
original order's verbatim and both are kept under `panel2_a6`.
